verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6 (worktree detached there, status clean, nothing added). glossary.mdx:319 (row 35): 'On a board of finite type, the root population at which no mutation raises any city.' This is the entry and the sentence of both findings. P6-RT-09-01's location (glossary.mdx:318-323, row 35), claim and observed (two root populations raised by no mutation on B2, B3, C3, F4, G2) contain all of P6-RT-13-01's claim; RT-09-01 adds row 36 (root poset). Oracle (python3 -I on copies of reference/ taken from f07eec6, positions): the positive roots p with mutate(C,p,i)[i] <= p[i] at every i are B2 [(1,1),(1,2)], B3 [(1,1,1),(1,2,2)], B4 [(1,1,1,1),(1,2,2,2)], C3 [(1,2,1),(2,2,1)], F4 [(1,2,3,2),(2,3,4,2)], G2 [(2,1),(3,2)]; 15 of the 31 distinct matrices have two (16 of the 32 named types counting B2 and C2 apart), and highest_root and highest_short_root return the larger and the smaller of each pair; golden kostant.B3.end_from_node = [[1,2,2],[1,2,2],[1,1,1]]. So the finding is right on the mathematics, and R1 to R5 fail: no passage permits the rule (SPEC 2.6 adds 'of largest form value'), the page is phase 6 at G6, the oracle sides with the finding, and there is no [D] or record. Only R6 holds. P6-RT-09-01's proposedFix ('the root population of largest form value at which no mutation raises any city (on a board with single roads, the only one)') is the fix RT-13-01 proposes. Note on R6's wording: RT-VERIFY 5.3 names the gate report or an earlier round's merge report as the record; here the record is the same round's confirmed finding, which the harness prompt points to. Dropping this finding loses nothing, because the fixer of P6-RT-09-01 receives the same entry and cause; RT-13-01's extra suggestion (name the highest short root in the entry) can go to that fixer as a note.
verdicts.reason: the same glossary entry (glossary.mdx:319, row 35) with the same cause, a rule that also picks out the highest short root on B, C, F and G, is already reported and confirmed in this round as P6-RT-09-01, and one cause gets one finding (RED-TEAM-COMMON 5); the oracle agrees with both findings, so nothing is lost by the merge.

verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because no passage lets a prediction's answer sit only in its reveal, and 4.0 Predict's <details> describes the fallback, not an exemption from P2. R2 failed, because P2 'Results are stated in the prose' has no qualifier. As in P5-RT-13-01 there is an ambiguity for the owner: neither answer is a result of SPEC 3 M9's figure table, and both can be derived. But ambiguity is not a permitting sentence. R3 failed, because M9 is phase 6 at G6. R4 failed, because the oracle gives (-1,-1,0) as the build does, so the dispute is where the value is stated, not what it is. R5 failed, because P6-A7's choice and M9.spec.ts:437 are a builder's record, not a [D] text, a section 10 default or an owner's answer, and the MERGE ruling covers only the replacement of the plan's predictions. R6 failed, because P5-RT-13-01 is recorded as fixed for M8 with a regression test for M8 alone, so M9 is a sibling recurrence in a new lesson with no record. Severity stays major, as 'a behaviour the specification states is missing'. It is not a blocker, because the answers sit in a <details> that opens without JavaScript.

Beat 4 (line 165) says 'the formula of beat 5 would give dim 𝔨 equal to 5'. Beat 5 (line 177) gives the two formulas, introduced as read-off rules 'verified by computation' (line 175). They compute the numbers but do not say what 𝔨 or 𝔭 is. Beat 7 (line 197) has 'equal data such as dim 𝔨 = ...', unlinked. The only sentence saying what 𝔨 and 𝔭 are is in the LieTheory paragraph (line 246, 'a Cartan involution θ and a decomposition 𝔨⊕𝔭'). glossary.mdx has no dfn for 𝔨 or 𝔭, and its 'character' entry (line 721) reads 'The number dim 𝔭 − dim 𝔨 of a real form.' Appendix C has no row for either. decisions/P6-A7.md, P6-A8.md, P6-terms.md and DECISIONS.md record no choice on defining them; P6-terms added rows only for M9's bold words compact, character, split form and quasi-split form. No other lens of this round reports the case (RT-08's coverage has no such finding). reports/gate-G6.md has no item on it. verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because no passage lets a term be used undefined in the primary reader's prose; SPEC 3 M9 beat 5 and the 2.15 wording of beat 4 require the notation dim 𝔨 but do not exempt it from 8.4. verdicts.reason: SPEC 4.0, 7.4 and 9.2 attach the caption to the tool's default state, and 6.6 lets a link change only the state keys it names, so a tool page reached from the Atlas keeps its default caption. That caption names A3 and is true of it (oracle and golden agree), T14's 'with that board loaded' is met, and the cause is P4-RT-13-04's, already refuted on these passages and held for the owner as a possible new requirement. The 447 links are new evidence for the owner, not a new defect.

verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because no passage permits a forward mention; beat 1's 'The data of beat 5' is a pointer, not a definition or a link. R2 failed, because the finding reads 8.4 correctly and the first use is in beat 1. R3 failed, because M9 is phase 6 at G6. R4 does not apply.
